summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted with right flank pain and diagnosed with an obstructing right ureteral stone causing pyelonephritis and E. coli bacteremia leading to sepsis. His hospital course was complicated by three episodes of sustained ventricular tachycardia requiring ICD shocks, likely triggered by the infection. He was treated with IV ceftriaxone, and a ureteral stent was placed to relieve obstruction. He developed C. difficile colitis, managed with oral vancomycin. His heart function declined, with a new echo showing LVEF 35–40%, and he was uptitrated on metoprolol after refusing amiodarone due to prior liver issues. His torsemide was held due to hypovolemia from infection and diarrhea. He stabilized, completed treatment, and was discharged to extended care for continued IV antibiotics and monitoring.
